spec: SPEC-WIRE-V3.md, proof-batch wire format v3 (consolidation edition)
retiredCorpus: ../proof-batch-v2/ — the complete frozen v2 fixture tree, kept as the pre-rotation record. The test that reads it to prove the backwards version gate against real v2 bytes is prover-side, on the shelf branch named in op-supernode/silhouette/README.md; on this branch the tree is the record, and the version gate is covered by the flipped-byte case here (retired-version-0x02).
publicValuesEncoding: alloy SolValue::abi_encode(&ProofBatch) == Solidity abi.encode(batch); a dynamic struct, so the first word is the offset 0x20
identifierNote: field ORDER is verbatim the stock Solidity `Identifier`; WIDTHS are narrowed to the ones CrossL2Inbox.calculateChecksum itself downcasts to, which is lossless because that function reverts above 2^64 / 2^32 / 2^64 before validateMessage can emit. `ExecMsg` is a STATIC struct (6 words, 192 bytes), so `ExecMsg[]` is a length word followed by the elements packed inline — no per-element offset words.
execMsgOrdering: execMsgs[] is a DEDUPLICATED SET, strictly increasing in the 192-byte canonical key (decision D17), enforced at decode. Dedup is on the FULL key, never on (chainId, blockNumber, logIndex): two entries sharing a coordinate but differing in origin, timestamp or msgHash are two contradictory assumptions and both must survive. See exec-msg-checksum-vectors.json for the key definition and an ordering vector.
outputRoot: keccak256(bytes32(0) || stateRoot || messagePasserStorageRoot || blockHash); derived, not on the wire. See output-root-vectors.json.

cases.name: empty-batch-invalid

cases.name: wrong-version-0x01
cases.expectedError: bad version 1, want 3 (v1 is retired: refuse, do not adapt)

cases.name: retired-version-0x02
cases.expectedError: bad version 2, want 3 (v2 is retired: refuse, do not adapt -- its BlockExport has six fields where v3 has seven)

cases.name: unknown-version-0x04
cases.expectedError: unknown version 4, want 3 (a higher version is refused, never best-effort decoded)

cases.name: bad-version
cases.expectedError: unknown version 255, want 3 (a higher version is refused, never best-effort decoded)

cases.name: decreasing-log-index

cases.name: bad-preimage-hash
cases.expectedError: invalid proof batch: blocks[0].logs[0] preimage hashes to 0x61d6138b161ac0a94e345e1f3c4a2f908630b8eb12d91c58fe670193f90cbe99, but logHash is 0xe862844726e267ebf46bcaee3a541b771a6c821808e87a497136d94f3cc5b09f

cases.name: short-preimage
cases.expectedError: invalid proof batch: blocks[0].logs[0] preimage is 19 bytes, must be 0 (absent) or at least 20 (address-prefixed)

cases.name: exec-msgs-unsorted

cases.name: exec-msgs-duplicate
cases.expectedError: invalid proof batch: blocks[0].execMsgs[1] duplicates its predecessor; execMsgs is a deduplicated set, strictly increasing in the canonical key

generative.name: idle-300-blocks
generative.description: 300 blocks — one 10-minute cadence at 2 s block time — exporting nothing and importing nothing. THE OPERATING POINT: chain P is private, so almost every block touches nothing cross-chain. This is the envelope the submitter actually sends.

recipe.scalars: keccak256("cove-fixture:idle-300-blocks:<field>") for prevOutputRoot, l1Head, rollupConfigHash, depSetHash; exportPolicyHash is the v2 default; newOutputRoot is the derived output root of the LAST block (decision D11)
recipe.blocks: for i in 0..300: blockNumber = 9500001 + i, timestamp = 1800900000 + 2*i, and blockHash / stateRoot / messagePasserStorageRoot = keccak256("cove-fixture:idle-300-blocks:<blockNumber>:<field>"); logs and execMsgs both empty (present as zero-length arrays, never elided)

generative.sizeNote: 320 bytes per block, nothing else. v2's equivalent was 77 101 bytes; the +19 200 is 300 blocks x 64, the offset word and length word of the new execMsgs array.

generative.name: max-realistic-300-blocks
generative.description: 300 blocks — exactly one 10-minute proof-batch cadence at 2 s block time — with 0/1/2 logs per block (300 logs total) and 0/1 imports per block (150 total), no preimages. The size case: this is what a production envelope looks like on wire v3. Not stored; build it from the recipe and check envelopeKeccak.

recipe.scalars: keccak256("cove-fixture:max-realistic-300-blocks:<field>") for prevOutputRoot, l1Head, rollupConfigHash, depSetHash; exportPolicyHash is the v2 default (keccak256("cove-export-v2:all-hashes"), unchanged by v3); newOutputRoot is NOT synthetic — it is the derived output root of the LAST block (decision D11)
recipe.blocks: for i in 0..300: blockNumber = 9000001 + i, timestamp = 1800200000 + 2*i, and blockHash / stateRoot / messagePasserStorageRoot = keccak256("cove-fixture:max-realistic-300-blocks:<blockNumber>:<field>")
recipe.logs: for j in 0..(i % 3): logIndex = j, logHash = keccak256("cove-fixture:max-realistic-300-blocks:log:<i>:<j>"), preimage empty
recipe.execMsgs: for j in 0..(i % 2): chainId = 424246, blockNumber = 500000 + i, logIndex = j, timestamp = 1800199900 + 2*i, origin = keccak256("origin:max-realistic-300-blocks:424246:<blockNumber>:<logIndex>")[12:], msgHash = keccak256("msgHash:max-realistic-300-blocks:424246:<blockNumber>:<logIndex>"); then sorted by the canonical key and deduplicated (decision D17)

generative.sizeNote: v3 costs 320 bytes per block, 160 per exported log and 192 per distinct executing message (v2: 256 per block, 160 per log, no import cost). THE FINDING: this case needs TWO blobs where its v2 equivalent needed one. The arithmetic, for a submitter sizing its transactions: 300 blocks at 320 = 96 000; +300 logs at 160 = 144 301 total, which already exceeds one blob (130 044) before any imports; +150 imports at 192 = 173 101. Multi-blob transactions have always been permitted — blobs concatenate in sidecar index order before decoding — but a submitter that assumed one blob per envelope must now count. The operating point is the `idle-300-blocks` case above, at 96 301 bytes in one blob. Preimage-bearing policies add the preimage length per log, padded to 32.
